name: Lost Hill
generated_description:
Lost Hill rises to 538 feet in Illinois. The Lost Hill Trail covers 1.9 miles with about 95 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 39.34971, -87.75167 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 225 miles north of Nashville, Tennessee. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Wolf Mound, Indian Mound and Bristol Hill — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.question: How long does it take to hike Lost Hill?
faqs.answer: The Lost Hill Trail is 1.9 miles with about 95 feet of elevation gain, and most hikers take roughly 0.5 hours of moving time. Add time for breaks and conditions — winter or wet weather can double the trip.

faqs.question: How hard is the Lost Hill hike?
faqs.answer: It's rated Easy using the National Park Service difficulty formula (1.9 miles, 95 ft of gain — about 50 ft of climbing per mile). The elevation profile on this page shows exactly where the steep sections fall.

faqs.question: Where is the Lost Hill trailhead?
faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 39.34971, -87.75167 in Illinois. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.question: Are dogs allowed on the Lost Hill trail?
faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Lost Hill?
faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is Lost Hill?
faqs.answer: Lost Hill stands at 538 feet (164 meters) in Illinois.
